faqs.q: How long does a tile roof last in Irvington, NJ?

runs.v: Clay tile can last 100 years or more and concrete tile typically 40 to 75 years, per InterNACHI and the Tile Roofing Industry Alliance; the underlayment fails first, so a 30-to-50-year-old tile roof often needs only new underlayment.

faqs.q: Should I repair or replace my Irvington tile roof?

runs.v: Repair localized damage; replace when broken tiles pass roughly 20–25% for clay or 15–20% for concrete, or the underlayment has failed across the roof (contractor rules of thumb).

faqs.q: Do you need a permit for tile roof work in Irvington, NJ?

runs.v: The New Jersey Uniform Construction Code governs roofing: re-covering a detached one- or two-family home is ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 with no permit. That is the 25% rule for roofing: on other buildings, work on more than 25% of the roof in 12 months needs a permit, as does structural work to carry tile, and plan review checks weight and wind-load requirements. The Township of Irvington construction office can clarify local requirements.

faqs.q: Does a tile roof in Irvington need historic-district approval?

runs.v: Confirm with the Township of Irvington construction office; properties in a historic district can need extra review. Per the National Park Service, National Register listing alone places no restriction on a private owner.

faqs.q: Can my Irvington home support the weight of a tile roof?

runs.v: Only a structural assessment can say, since tile weighs far more than asphalt, and reinforcing the framing needs a permit.
